title: Patch: the AI prices Trample's excess and Lifesteal's healing when it weighs an attack on a unit

**Issue #1820 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1820: Patch: the AI prices Trample's excess and Lifesteal's healing when it weighs an attack on a unit
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The practice AI judges an attack on a unit by what the strike removes — but two things the rules add to every hit are missing from the price. A Trample attacker's overflow damage keeps going into the enemy hero, and a Lifesteal hit heals its own hero — including the defender's strike-back, which heals the defending hero and should count against the trade. Today the AI undervalues Trample attacks on small units and Lifesteal attackers' hits, and misjudges attacks into Lifesteal defenders. After this change the trade price counts all four.

## Why

`trade_value` (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:112-127`) prices kill worth, chip damage, the shield pop, the attacker's own death and Cleave splash — nothing else. Two damage-pipeline riders are missing:

- **Trample** — SPEC §4.4 step 9 sends dealt-minus-health to the defender's hero. The AI's threat model already prices it (`evaluate.rs:688-690` calls `subsystems::projected_hero_damage` on the excess), and `reply_face_value` (`reply.rs:132-138`) is the right helper to reuse.
- **Lifesteal** — §6.1: dealt damage heals the dealer's hero, and dealt is not capped at the target's health (§4.4 step 5). A 7-attack Lifesteal unit hitting a 2-health unit heals 7; a Lifesteal defender's strike-back heals the other side's hero the same way. Neither direction is priced.

The misprice is load-bearing: `ranked_attacks` (`reply.rs:170`) picks the opponent's simulated best reply, so every searched finalist is scored against a reply the real opponent would not make, and `even_trade` (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:316`) picks the AI's own best trade. (Rejected #1637 was the My Pawn lethal solver's strike-back read — a different function.)

## Proposal

Inside `trade_value` only: add `reply_face_value(state, target.controller, dealt - t.view.health)` when the excess is positive and the attacker has Trample, and add a heal term for each side's Lifesteal strike — `hero_value(h + dealt) - hero_value(h)` — exposing `hero_value` as `pub(crate)` or adding a small `heal_worth` helper beside `evaluate.rs:55-60`. Compute the damage instance's amount separately where `blow.dealt` short-circuits: an Indestructible target still takes the instance (§4.4 step 5), so Trample still spills.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/`. The decision layer only; engine and spec untouched, numbers stay named constants (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Trample attacker's `trade_value` exceeds plain kill worth when the excess reaches the hero.
- [ ] A Lifesteal attacker's heal on its hit, and a Lifesteal defender's strike-back heal, each move the price in the right direction.
- [ ] A `ranked_attacks` ordering test: at low life the Lifesteal trade outranks a plain face hit.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` smoke reports no regression.

## Size and risks

Medium: ~30 lines plus tests in one crate. The usual AI-tuning risk — the gate's screen decides whether the better model wins more — mitigated by the change pricing real rules effects, not a new heuristic.

---

## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40160376850)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Goal.** The static trader's `trade_value` (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`) prices two damage-pipeline riders it ignores today: a Trample attacker's excess that reaches the defender's hero (SPEC §4.4 step 9) and the heal a Lifesteal attacker's hits give its own hero (§4.4 step 8, uncapped by the target's health, step 5). Done when a Trample kill is worth more than the bare kill, a Lifesteal hit is worth the heal of all it deals, `ranked_attacks` puts a Lifesteal trade above a plain face hit at low life (and not at full life), and every check is green. The fourth item, the **defender's** Lifesteal strike-back heal, is held back for a person: with it, `b18_p9` goes red (see Open questions).

**Files to touch.**

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs` | change | new `pub(crate) fn heal_worth` after `hero_value`; `heal_multiplier_of` added to the `jackioh_engine` import |
| `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` | change | `trade_value`: `lands`, `trample`, `on_unit`, `splashed`, `trampled`, the Lifesteal term; imports; doc comment; seven tests in `mod tests` |
| `crates/ai/README.md` | change | one clause in the `decide` paragraph (lines 66-67) |
| `docs/polish/3-ai.md` | change | one sentence in step 3 of the reply rule (after line 719) |

Do not touch:
- `crates/engine` or `crates/cards`.
- `spec/`. No ruling is added.
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs`. No new weight is needed: the face price is `AI_REPLY.face_per_damage`, and the heal uses the hero curve.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/puzzles.rs` or any other test file.

Governing rules: SPEC §4.3 (First Strike order; R783000, Ranged), §4.4 steps 1, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 10, R63, R176, R1750000 (a strike back never tramples), R1180003 (the healing multiplier), and §6.3 (a hero's heal has no cap).

Rejected from the issue: "an Indestructible target still takes the instance, so Trample still spills". §4.4 step 4 reads "Indestructible: takes no damage; stop", and `crates/engine/src/damage.rs` returns before steps 5 and 9 (lines 531-539), as `subsystems::lethal::trample_excess` does. So `blow`'s `dealt == 0` for an Indestructible or shielded target is correct and stays, and a test holds it.

**Steps.**

1. `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`: in the `use jackioh_engine::{…}` list add `heal_multiplier_of` (after `has_keyword`). Right after `fn hero_value` (which ends at line 60) add:

```rust
/// §4.4 step 8: what healing `player`'s hero by `amount` is worth on `hero_value`'s curve, the more the
/// lower its life, its healing multiplier included (R1180003). A hero's heal has no cap (§6.3).
pub(crate) fn heal_worth(state: &GameState, player: PlayerId, amount: i32, w: &EvalWeights) -> f64 {
    let life = effective_life(state, player);
    if amount <= 0 || life <= 0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let start = starting_life(state, player);
    let healed = amount.saturating_mul(heal_multiplier_of(state, player));
    hero_value(life.saturating_add(healed), start, w) - hero_value(life, start, w)
}
```

2. `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` imports: add `AttackTarget` to the `jackioh_engine` list, `Side` to `use crate::candidates::{…}` and `heal_worth` to `use crate::evaluate::{…}`.

3. In `trade_value`, right after the `if t.first_strike && !a.first_strike && dies { kills = false; }` block, add:

```rust
    // §4.3 step 1: an attacker a First Strike defender destroys first strikes nothing at all.
    let lands = !(t.first_strike && !a.first_strike && dies);
    // §4.4 step 5: a Trample attacker's hit counts on a unit only up to its health, the rest being step
    // 9's hit on the hero.
    let trample = has_keyword(&a.view.keywords, KeywordKind::Trample);
    let on_unit = |dealt: i32, to: &Side| {
        if trample {
            dealt.min(to.view.health.max(0))
        } else {
            dealt
        }
    };
```

4. In the Cleave block:
   - after `let mut cleave_value = 0.0;` add `let mut splashed = 0;`;
   - change its condition `!(t.first_strike && !a.first_strike && dies)` to `lands`;
   - right after `let splash = blow(…);` add `splashed += on_unit(splash.dealt, &n);`.

   Nothing else in the loop changes.

5. After the `if dies { value -= kill_worth(…); }` block, before `Trade {`, add:

```rust
    // §4.4 step 9: what the attack's hits deal beyond each unit's health goes on to the target's hero
    // through its Armor and caps (`projected_damage`: a Cleave's hits too, R176, and nothing when a
    // First Strike defender destroys the attacker first).
    let trampled = if trample {
        subsystems::projected_damage(
            state,
            attacker,
            &AttackTarget::Unit {
                instance: target.clone(),
            },
        )
    } else {
        0
    };
    if trampled > 0 {
        value += reply_face_value(state, target.controller, trampled);
    }
    // §4.4 step 8: Lifesteal heals the attacker's hero by what each of its hits deals, which step 5 does
    // not cap at the unit's health but for a Trample hit, whose rest heals as it lands on the hero.
    if lands && has_keyword(&a.view.keywords, KeywordKind::Lifesteal) {
        value += heal_worth(
            state,
            attacker.controller,
            on_unit(out.dealt, &t) + splashed + trampled,
            &AI_EVAL,
        );
    }
```

6. `trade_value`'s doc comment: after the sentence ending "…the same share of the Divine Shield weight." insert: "A Trample attacker's hits add what they land beyond each struck unit's health on the target's hero, priced as a face hit (`reply_face_value`, §4.4 step 9), and a Lifesteal attacker's add what healing its own hero by all they deal is worth (`heal_worth`, step 8; #1820)."

7. `crates/ai/README.md`, lines 66-67: change "(a unit with Reborn unspent less the body it comes back as, #1796)" to "(a unit with Reborn unspent less the body it comes back as, #1796; plus a Trample attacker's excess on the hero and a Lifesteal attacker's heal, #1820)", and rewrap to the paragraph's width.

8. `docs/polish/3-ai.md`, step 3 of the reply rule: after "…less the attacker's own, priced the same way, if it dies." insert "A Trample attacker's hits add `facePerDamage` per point they land beyond each struck unit's health on the hero (`projectedDamage`, §4.4 step 9), and a Lifesteal attacker's add what healing its own hero by all they deal is worth on the hero curve (step 8, #1820)." Rewrap.

9. Run `cargo fmt`.

**Tests.** All of them go in `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`'s `mod tests`. `trade_value` and `ranked_attacks` are crate-private, so `crates/ai/tests/` cannot reach them, and #1796's tests already sit there.

Set up the module:
- Change its import to `use jackioh_engine::testkit::{Keyword, Scenario, Value, json, scenario};` and add `use jackioh_engine::config::HERO_HEALTH;`.
- After `VANILLA`, add three constants, each with a doc line like the others:
  - `OOMEN = "core-067"` (Zoomerbin Oomen, 1/2);
  - `POINTMASTER = "core-020"` (7/1 First Strike);
  - `LIFE_MAGE = "meditativeplus-007"` (its Radiant face makes healing twice as effective, R1180003).
- Add these helpers:

```rust
    /// `setup`'s scenario with `keywords` granted to its Mr. Vanilla.
    fn vanilla_with(setup: Value, keywords: &[Keyword]) -> Scenario {
        jackioh_cards::register_all();
        let mut s = scenario(setup);
        s.card_mut(VANILLA).granted_keywords.extend_from_slice(keywords);
        s
    }

    /// What healing a 1v1 hero at `life` by `amount` is worth on `hero_value`'s curve.
    fn healed(life: i32, amount: i32) -> f64 {
        let start = f64::from(HERO_HEALTH);
        AI_EVAL.hero_health * ((f64::from(life + amount) * start).sqrt() - (f64::from(life) * start).sqrt())
    }
```

How each `trade_value` test works:
- Build the board with `vanilla_with`, call `trade_value(s.state(), s.card(VANILLA), &s.card(<target>).id)`, and assert `(trade.value - expected).abs() < 1e-9` with the message `"{}", trade.value`, like the existing tests.
- `kill_worth(oomen)` below means `kill_worth(s.state(), s.card(OOMEN), &AI_EVAL)`; `kill_worth(vanilla)` likewise.
- Unless stated, the board is the first test's, with the stated keys added.

The tests:
- `a_trample_kill_adds_the_excess_it_lands_on_the_hero`
  - Board `{"p1":{"field":[VANILLA]},"p2":{"field":[OOMEN]}}`, keywords `[Keyword::Trample]`.
  - Assert `trade.kills`, expected `kill_worth(oomen) + AI_REPLY.face_per_damage * 2.0`, and `trade.value > kill_worth(oomen)`.
- `an_indestructible_target_lets_no_trample_through`
  - Same board, bound with `let mut s`, then `s.card_mut(OOMEN).granted_keywords.push(Keyword::Indestructible)`.
  - Assert `!trade.kills` and `trade.value.abs() < 1e-9`.
- `a_lifesteal_hit_is_worth_the_heal_of_all_it_deals`
  - p1 `"health": 10`, keywords `[Keyword::Lifesteal]`.
  - Assert `trade.kills`; expected `kill_worth(oomen) + healed(10, 4)`, because all 4 dealt heal, not just the Oomen's 2 health.
- `a_trample_lifesteal_hit_heals_what_lands_on_the_unit_and_on_the_hero`
  - p1 health 10, p2 `"armor": 1`, keywords `[Keyword::Trample, Keyword::Lifesteal]`.
  - Expected `kill_worth(oomen) + AI_REPLY.face_per_damage * 1.0 + healed(10, 3)`: 2 land on the Oomen, 2 trample on, and the Armor takes 1.
- `a_healing_multiplier_doubles_the_lifesteal_heal_it_prices`
  - p1 health 10, p1 field `[VANILLA, {"def": LIFE_MAGE, "radiant": true}]`, keywords `[Keyword::Lifesteal]`.
  - Expected `kill_worth(oomen) + healed(10, 8)`.
- `an_attacker_a_first_strike_defender_destroys_first_heals_nothing`
  - p1 health 10, p2 field `[POINTMASTER]`, keywords `[Keyword::Lifesteal]`.
  - Assert `!trade.kills`; expected `AI_REPLY.chip_per_damage * 1.0 - kill_worth(vanilla)`. Today's chip on the 1 health stays, and nothing heals.

The ordering test, `at_low_life_the_lifesteal_trade_outranks_a_plain_face_hit`:
- Helper `fn best_reply_attack(health: i32) -> (Scenario, ActionBody)`:
  - board `vanilla_with({"active":"p2","p1":{"field":[OOMEN]},"p2":{"health":health,"field":[VANILLA,{"def":CURVATURE,"radiant":true}]}}, &[Keyword::Lifesteal])`;
  - best attack `ranked_attacks(s.state(), PlayerId::P1, &legal_actions(s.state(), PlayerId::P2), false).into_iter().next().expect("an attack worth making")`.
- At `best_reply_attack(3)` the best is `ActionBody::Attack { attacker_id: <Vanilla id>, target_id: <Oomen id> }`: 3.2 + 5.0 against the Curvature's 6.0.
- At `best_reply_attack(HERO_HEALTH)` the best is the Curvature on `"hero-p1"`: 3.2 + 1.9 < 6.0.

I built exactly these steps in a scratch copy:
- All ten `reply::tests` pass.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes 20 + 565 + 82 tests.
- The workspace tests pass. One tools acceptance test needs a git checkout, and passed once the copy had one.
- clippy and fmt are clean, and `spec check` passes.

Commands to run:

```
cargo test -p jackioh-ai reply::tests
cargo test -p jackioh-ai
cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
cargo jackioh spec check
cargo jackioh gate
cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims
```

**Done when.**
- [ ] The seven new tests and the three existing `reply::tests` pass. All but `an_indestructible_…` and `an_attacker_a_first_strike_…` (which guard the rejected claim and `lands`) fail on `main`'s `trade_value`; I confirmed this.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes, including `b18_p9…`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/cleave.rs`, `even_trades.rs` and `ranged_flying.rs`, with no test edited outside `reply.rs`.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) passes, and its three quality lines are quoted in the PR body. My runs read the same on `main` and on this change:
  - ai-vs-random 19 of 20 (17 needed);
  - ai-vs-greedy 20 of 20 (10 needed);
  - hard-vs-easy 17 of 20 (16 needed).

  If it fails, report it by name and stop: no weight is tuned to pass it.
- [ ] rustfmt, clippy, the workspace tests, spec check (the cited R63, R176, R1750000 and R1180003 exist), and the catalog and patches checks are green.
- [ ] `classify --claims` reports no card that plays differently. An AI change needs no patch fragment; #1813 had none.
- [ ] The PR body records the decisions under Risks, the rejected Indestructible claim and the held-back defender term.

**Risks.**
- **Determinism and hidden information:** the new reads (`projected_damage`, `effective_life`, `heal_multiplier_of`) read the public board through the engine's pure helpers. Nothing reads a hand or library, so R185 holds.
- **Cost:** `projected_damage` clones the target once and runs only for a Trample attacker. `trade_value` is called for every attack at every reply step, so this matters.
- **Decisions recorded:**
  - The Trample excess is read through `subsystems::projected_damage` instead of the issue's `dealt - t.view.health`. The engine's projection also covers the hero's Armor and caps, a Cleave's trample (R176) and the First Strike case.
  - The heal includes the healing multiplier (§4.4 step 8, R1180003), which the issue left out.
  - The face branch of `ranked_attacks` stays unpriced for Lifesteal, because the issue scopes the change to `trade_value`.
- **Lethal Trample:** `reply_face_value` prices a lethal Trample excess at `AI_EVAL.win` even when a Lifesteal defender's strike back would outheal it (R176's case, which `subsystems::is_lethal` handles). This is rare and left as is.
- **Duos:** `heal_worth` adds the heal to `effective_life` uncapped, while a spent Duos hero's pool heals only up to its cap (#936 B14). The Duos AI slightly over-prices that heal. Left as is.

**Open questions.**
- **The defender's Lifesteal strike-back heal (the second half of acceptance item 2) needs a person.**
  - What I tried: in the scratch copy I built the full design, subtracting `heal_worth(state, target.controller, <strike-back dealt>, &AI_EVAL)` when the strike back lands.
  - What broke: `crates/ai/tests/ai/puzzles.rs`'s `b18_p9_at_5_health_with_an_empty_board_jilliax_goes_down_to_block_4_plus_3_and_p1_survives_the_swing_back` fails. It passes on `main`, and passes again with only that term removed.
  - Why the AI's line changes: in P9 the AI can play Jilliax and attack Tempo Timmy. In the reply, the Deft Duelist's trade into the Lifesteal Jilliax is worth +0.1 on `main` (8.4 − 8.3). Any heal price makes it negative (the heal is worth 2.67 at the AI's 8 life). The static trader then stops attacking, so the AI takes that line.
  - Why the test goes red: the scripted all-out swing trades anyway, leaving p1 at 11 with both boards and both libraries empty. R82 then auto-ends every turn inside that one `reduce`, and fatigue kills p1 before p2 (at 29).
  - The choice for a person: drop the term, or add it and change P9's setup so that fatigue race cannot happen inside the swing (give both sides a library, which also changes P9's row in `docs/polish/3-ai.md`). The bot may not change a puzzle to reach green.
````
